_README: Physical materials we alter. Copied from vanilla and patched, so the mod's
PM_SnowRoad is the one that matters. Arini's ground is Mat_Road_Snow on 38 of
64 ground/path meshes, and that material's PhysMaterial is PM_SnowRoad -- NOT
PM_Snow. PM_SnowRoad has no digging properties at all: it is a road surface,
friction 0.4, rolling resistance 2. Three rounds of patching PM_Snow changed
nothing because nothing on the island uses it.
A Vector2D is written as (X;Y) with a SEMICOLON -- --set splits its pairs on
commas, so a comma there would be read as two properties.
This edits VANILLA PM_SnowRoad, so every snow road in Jeju digs too. That is
deliberate for now: feel the numbers first, then move them to a new material
applied only where wanted and swap our meshes over to it.

materials._: Every property here is absent in vanilla: PM_SnowRoad is a ROAD surface with no digging block at all, and an absent property is its default -- zero for a float, false for a bool. bIsOffroad is the GATE; without it none of the rest is read. DELIBERATELY PAST VANILLA: the deepest surface in the game is Sand at (5,35) speed 2 resist 6, and MudPuddle's exact numbers (5,20)/2/3 still read as 'not sinking enough'. (12.5,50) speed 3 resist 2 -- (10,40) read as 'good, 25% more and it's perfect', so this is that 25%. Far past vanilla's deepest (Sand, (5,35)) -- if this is dramatic, dial back; if it is still subtle, the limit is not in these numbers and the question becomes whether digging works on static-mesh roads at all. SurfaceType is NOT the gate (Dirt digs at 2, Sand at 10, Mud at 11), so it stays 7.

Kept from the earlier rounds. PM_Snow already declares bAllowDigging and depth (1,5) and only lacks the two gates. Nothing on Arini references it today, but deep-snow surfaces elsewhere do, and the patch costs one asset.
